use_case: Track and equipment defect detection (computer vision): a camera rig on a hi-rail inspection vehicle and one wayside camera portal on the North Subdivision flag suspected track, joint, tie, fastener, and car component defects for human review
vendor_or_model: Defect detection vendor (licensed computer vision model run as an inference service in the company cloud tenant)
data_categories: Images and video of track, bridges, grade crossings, and passing rail cars; GPS location and milepost; inspector review decisions. Incidental images of employees, trespassers, and the public at crossings
affects_individuals: Yes (indirectly: train crews, roadway workers, and the public depend on track and equipment safety; incidental images of people)
human_in_the_loop: A qualified track inspector designated under 49 CFR 213.7 reviews every model flag and still performs every required visual inspection; car flags go to a qualified mechanical inspector. The model never clears a defect or closes an inspection
applicable_laws: 49 CFR 213.233(b) (inspection devices only supplement visual inspection); 49 CFR 213.7; 49 CFR 215.13 (pre-departure car inspection); 49 CFR 1520.9 if imagery reveals security measures marked SSI; Fla. Stat. 501.171 not triggered (no personal information stored)
status: Pilot (North Subdivision since 2026-03); expansion to the South Subdivision on hold until conditions in section 6 are met

use_case: General-purpose generative AI chatbots used by office staff to draft letters and summaries
data_categories: Risk of Restricted data or SSI being pasted (customer contracts, network details, hazmat plan text)
risk_tier: Low (Medium if Restricted data or SSI is entered)
applicable_laws: 49 CFR 1520.9(a) (SSI may be disclosed only to covered persons with a need to know); POL-04 and POL-05 4.8
status: Prohibited for Restricted data and SSI (POL-05 4.8); enterprise tool under evaluation for 2027
